note: Agents MUST load the listed module before writing each surface (APPLY, not prefer). CGM does not CI-enforce prose style; presence of modules + this contract is what validate_content_system checks. ACS should inject required_load / apply_checklist into agent prompts on hotload (see acs_prompt_inject).

routes.notes: Keep scan-first selective bold and the README scanability contract.
Human voice, AI-tell scrub, restrained bold. Includes chart/takeaway guidance for papers and data writeups. Commit messages and commit subjects are in scope — MUST load hsw before writing them.

apply_checklist: Identify the writing surface (README, PR title/body, issue title/body, issue-log title, commit message/subject, non-README doc, changelog prose, post/blog/social, paper/data writeup).
Look up the surface in routes[].surfaces in docs/writing-routing.json (or the table in docs/WRITING_ROUTING.md).
MUST load modules/<load>/SKILL.md for that route before drafting — required_load is true; do not skip because the surface is short or 'just a commit'.
Apply the module rules to the draft (voice, AI-tell scrub, bold policy as the module states).
README / product entry stays on writing-direction; do not apply hsw bold restraints there.

acs_prompt_inject.when: After hotload_check / CGM_VERIFY succeeds, before the agent writes human-facing GitHub or docs prose.
acs_prompt_inject.instruction: Inject into the agent system or task prompt: For every route with required_load true, you MUST load modules/<load>/SKILL.md before writing any listed surface. README and product entry pages → writing-direction. Pull request titles/bodies, issue titles/bodies, issue-log titles, commit messages, commit subjects, non-README docs, changelog prose, posts/blogs/social/general prose, and papers/data writeups → human-sounding-writing (hsw). Soft enforcement means no NLP CI grade of prose; the contract language is MUST/APPLY, not prefer. Follow apply_checklist in this file.
